examples.en: My older brother works as a resident at the hospital.

examples.ko: 레지던트는 밤에도 당직을 서는 일이 많아요.
examples.en: Residents often take night duty too.
After graduating from medical school, I passed the residency exam.
The resident doctor examined the patient first.
He finished his pediatrics residency.

examples.ko: 드라마에는 잠도 못 자는 레지던트가 자주 나와요.
examples.en: Sleepless residents often appear in dramas.

explain: 인턴을 마치고 한 과를 전문으로 배우는 수련 중인 의사를 말해요. 한국에서는 '인턴, 레지던트, 전문의' 순서로 올라가요. 환자에게는 보통 '선생님'이라고 부르고 '레지던트'는 병원 안 직급 이름이에요.

phrases.en: My friend works as a resident at a university hospital.
phrases.nuance_ko: 직업을 말할 때 가장 자연스러운 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most natural way to state this job.

phrases.en: I'm now a first-year resident.
phrases.nuance_ko: 수련 몇 년째인지 말할 때 '1년차, 2년차'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add 1년차, 2년차 to say which year of training it is.

phrases.example: 인턴과 레지던트는 모두 수련 중인 의사예요.
phrases.en: Interns and residents are both doctors in training.
phrases.nuance_ko: 함께 배우는 의사 단계를 말할 때 짝으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used together for the stages of doctors in training.

explain_en: Loanword for a hospital doctor in specialty training, spoken. A doctor in training who has finished an internship and is learning a specialty. In Korea the order is 인턴, 레지던트, 전문의. Patients simply say 선생님; 레지던트 is a rank used inside the hospital.

t90.ax: Residents often take night duty too.

examples.ko: 이 상을 받게 되어 정말 명예로워요.
examples.en: I'm truly honored to receive this award.
He retired with honor.
Defending the country is an honorable job.
I think we lost with honor.
The players can't forget the honorable moment.
It's an honorable position, but it carries heavy responsibility.

explain: 사람들에게 존경받을 만하거나 자랑스러운 일·자리·행동에 써요. 평범한 기쁨에는 어울리지 않아요. 상을 받거나 큰 역할을 맡을 때 '영광이에요'와 같이 격식 있게 말해요. 'ㅂ 불규칙'이라 '명예로워요'로 바뀌어요.

phrases.en: Being chosen as the representative is an honor.
phrases.nuance_ko: ㅂ 불규칙이라 '명예로운'으로 바뀌어 명사를 꾸며요.
phrases.nuance_en: As a ㅂ-irregular adjective, it becomes '명예로운' to modify a noun.

phrases.en: A prize won by lying is not honorable.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자랑스럽지 못하고 존경받기 어려운 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for something not worth being proud of or respected for.

phrases.en: It is an honor to stand here.
phrases.nuance_ko: '명예롭다'와 비슷한 뜻이고, 상을 받거나 큰 역할을 맡았을 때 격식 있게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Close in meaning, used formally when receiving a prize or a big role.

explain_en: For jobs, positions or deeds that earn respect and pride; it doesn't suit ordinary happiness. When receiving an award or a big role it works like '영광이에요' in formal speech. It is a ㅂ-irregular adjective, so it becomes '명예로워요'.

p.n: Nearly identical; 명예스럽다 is the rarer variant.

examples.ko: 아버지는 목공을 배워서 책상을 직접 만드셨어요.
examples.en: My father learned woodworking and made the desk himself.
I attend a woodworking class every weekend.
Woodworking is my hobby, so I have many tools at home.
Simple woodworking needs a saw and a hammer.
The bookshelf made by woodworking looks sturdy.

examples.ko: 목공은 정확하게 재는 게 가장 중요하다고 들었어요.
examples.en: I heard that measuring accurately is the most important thing in woodworking.

explain: 나무로 물건을 만드는 일을 가리키고, 그 일을 하는 사람은 보통 '목수'라고 불러요. 요즘은 가구나 소품을 직접 만드는 취미로도 많이 얘기해요.

phrases.en: I bought new woodworking tools.
phrases.nuance_ko: 톱, 망치처럼 나무 작업에 쓰는 도구를 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to tools like saws and hammers used for woodwork.

phrases.en: I made a chair at a woodworking studio near my home.
phrases.nuance_ko: 목공을 하거나 배우는 작업 공간을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A workspace where people do or learn woodworking.

phrases.en: I do woodworking as a hobby.
phrases.nuance_ko: 직업이 아니라 즐기는 활동으로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when it is an enjoyed activity, not a job.
phrases.en_equiv: to do woodwork as a hobby

explain_en: It refers to the work of making things from wood, and the person who does it is usually called a '목수'. Today it is also talked about as a hobby of making furniture and small items yourself.

examples.en: My father is a carpenter who has worked for a long time.
A carpenter came and fixed the door.
A famous carpenter made this chair.

examples.ko: 저는 나중에 목수가 되어서 집을 짓고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to become a carpenter and build houses later.
The carpenter is cutting wood.

examples.ko: 한옥을 짓는 목수는 특별한 기술이 필요해요.
examples.en: A carpenter who builds hanok needs special skills.

explain: 목수는 나무로 집이나 가구를 만드는 사람이에요. 직접 부를 때는 보통 '목수님'이라고 해요. 한국어에서 나무를 다루는 일은 '목공'이라고도 하고, '목공 수업', '목공 체험'처럼 써요.

phrases.example: 목수님, 이 문 좀 봐 주세요.
phrases.en: Mr. Carpenter, please take a look at this door.
phrases.nuance_ko: 직접 부를 때는 '님'을 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add 님 when addressing someone directly.

phrases.en: My father has worked as a carpenter for a long time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 직업으로 목수가 하는 일을 한다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say someone does carpentry work as a job.

phrases.en: I want to become a carpenter someday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 꿈이나 직업 이야기에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when talking about dreams or jobs.

explain_en: 목수 is a person who builds houses or furniture out of wood. When addressing one directly, people usually say 목수님. Working with wood is also called 목공, as in 목공 수업 or 목공 체험.

en: to belong to; to be affiliated with; to work in

examples.ko: 저는 십 년 동안 이 회사에 몸담았어요.
examples.en: I worked at this company for ten years.

examples.ko: 교육 분야에 몸담고 있는 분을 만났어요.
examples.en: I met someone who works in the field of education.

examples.ko: 옛날 자신이 몸담았던 부대를 보자 반가웠어요.
examples.en: He felt glad when he saw the unit he used to belong to.
Which club are you a member of?

examples.ko: 몸담은 지 오래된 곳이라 정이 많이 들었어요.
examples.en: I've been part of this place for a long time, so I've grown attached to it.

examples.ko: 그 일에 몸담으면서 많은 걸 배웠어요.
examples.en: I learned a lot while working in that field.

explain: '회사에 몸담다', '이 분야에 몸담다'처럼 '에'와 함께 써요. 단순히 '일하다'보다 그 조직이나 분야에 속해 오래 있었다는 느낌이 있고, 조금 격식 있게 들려요.

phrases.en: He has been in the medical field for a long time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금도 그 분야에서 일하고 있다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means the person is still working in that field.

phrases.en: The place where I used to work was a small company.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금은 떠난 조직이나 회사를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for an organization or company you have left.

phrases.example: 삼 년째 이 회사에서 근무하고 있어요.
phrases.en: I've been working at this company for three years.
phrases.nuance_ko: '몸담다'보다 일반적이고, 직장에서 일한다는 사실만 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: More neutral than 몸담다; it just states that you work at a workplace.

explain_en: Belonging through long work or career, warmer feel (회사에 몸담다) It is used with '에', as in '회사에 몸담다' or '이 분야에 몸담다'. Compared with plain '일하다', it suggests belonging to that organization or field for a while, and it sounds a bit formal.

examples.ko: 무직자는 대출 심사가 더 까다로울 수 있어요.
examples.en: Loan screening can be stricter for people without a job.

examples.ko: 저는 지금 무직자지만 곧 취직할 거예요.
examples.en: I'm unemployed right now, but I'll get a job soon.

examples.ko: 무직자도 청년 지원금을 신청할 수 있대요.
examples.en: I heard even people without jobs can apply for the youth support fund.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 무직자라서 카드를 만들기 어려웠어요.
examples.en: He had no job, so it was hard for him to get a card.
I gathered job information that unemployed people need.

examples.ko: 무직자 비율이 조금 줄었다는 기사가 나왔어요.
examples.en: An article came out saying the share of people without jobs fell slightly.

explain: 서류나 통계에서 '직업: 무직'처럼 쓰는 딱딱한 말이라, 사람에게 직접 쓰면 차갑게 들릴 수 있어요. 일자리를 찾는 사람은 '구직자'라고 해요.

phrases.en: I wrote 'unemployed' for my occupation on the form.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서류나 통계에서 직업이 없는 상태를 적을 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used on forms or in statistics to state having no occupation.

phrases.en: I'm worried because I've been without a job for so long.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일이 없는 기간이나 상황을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when talking about a period or situation of having no job.

phrases.en: There is free training for job seekers.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일자리를 찾는 사람을 말하며 '무직자'보다 부드럽게 들려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to people looking for work and sounds gentler than '무직자'.

explain_en: It is a stiff word from forms and statistics, as in '직업: 무직', so using it directly about a person can sound cold. A person looking for work is called a '구직자' (job seeker).

examples.en: Einstein is a famous physicist.
My dream is to become a physicist.
Physicists discovered a new particle.

examples.ko: 그 물리학자는 우주에 대한 책을 썼어요.
examples.en: That physicist wrote a book about the universe.
My uncle is a physicist who works at a university.
The news interviewed a physicist.

explain: '과학자'가 넓은 이름이고, 물리학자·화학자·수학자는 분야별로 부르는 이름이에요. 대학 전공은 '물리학과'(또는 '물리 전공'), 연구하는 직업은 '물리학자'라고 구분해서 말해요. 소리, 빛, 힘, 에너지처럼 자연의 움직임을 다루는 사람에게 써요.

phrases.en: My older brother studies physics at university.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 아니라 대학의 전공을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the university major, not the person.

phrases.en: A physicist is one kind of scientist.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과학자는 넓은 이름이고 물리학자는 그 안의 한 분야예요.
phrases.nuance_en: 과학자 is the broad term and 물리학자 is one field within it.

phrases.en: Physicists study the universe.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 사람을 말할 때 '-들'을 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add -들 when talking about several people.

explain_en: 과학자 is the broad word, and 물리학자, 화학자, and 수학자 name the specific fields. A university major is 물리학과 (or 물리 전공), while the working scientist is a 물리학자. It is used for people who study motion, light, force, and energy.

examples.en: Every dawn, the sanitation worker cleans the street.
I always feel grateful to the sanitation workers.

examples.ko: 우리 학교 미화원 선생님은 항상 웃으며 인사해 주세요.
examples.en: Our school's cleaning staff member always greets us with a smile.

examples.ko: 비가 오는 날에도 미화원들은 쉬지 않고 일해요.
examples.en: Even on rainy days, sanitation workers keep working without a break.

examples.ko: 쓰레기를 분리해서 버리면 미화원이 일하기 편해요.
examples.en: If you sort your trash, it's easier for sanitation workers.

examples.ko: 아파트 미화원이 계단을 깨끗하게 닦아 주셨어요.
examples.en: The apartment cleaner wiped the stairs clean.

explain: 길이나 건물을 깨끗하게 하는 일을 하는 분을 정중하게 부르는 말이에요. 요즘은 '청소부'보다 '미화원'이 더 정중하게 들려요. 직접 부를 때는 '아저씨', '선생님'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: The sanitation workers start working early in the morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: '분'을 붙여서 더 존중하는 느낌으로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 분 makes it sound more respectful.

phrases.en: I greeted the sanitation worker.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공식적으로 이 직업을 말할 때 쓰는 이름이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The official name for this job.

phrases.en: The street cleaner is sweeping the road.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻은 같지만 '미화원'이 더 정중하게 들려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning, but 미화원 sounds more polite.

explain_en: Shortened everyday form of the full job title (환경미화원); same job, same meaning. It is a polite term for people who keep streets and buildings clean. These days '미화원' sounds more respectful than '청소부'. When addressing someone directly, people say '아저씨' or '선생님'.

en: to be knowledgeable; to be erudite

examples.ko: 우리 선생님은 역사에 대해 정말 박식하세요.
examples.en: Our teacher is really knowledgeable about history.

examples.ko: 박식한 사람과 이야기하면 배울 게 많아요.
examples.en: When you talk with a knowledgeable person, there is a lot to learn.

examples.ko: 그는 커피에 박식해서 추천을 잘해 줘요.
examples.en: He knows a lot about coffee, so he gives good recommendations.

examples.ko: 박식하다는 평을 듣지만 잘난 척하지 않아요.
examples.en: He is said to be well read, but he doesn't show off.
Grandfather is so knowledgeable that there is nothing he doesn't know.
You're so knowledgeable, so why do you say you don't know?

explain: 책이나 공부로 폭넓게 지식을 쌓은 사람에게 하는 칭찬이에요. 보통 '~에 박식하다'처럼 '에'와 함께 쓰고, 높일 때는 '박식하시다'예요. '해박하다'도 비슷한 뜻으로 쓰여요.

phrases.en: Thanks to my knowledgeable friend, the homework was easy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸미는 활용형으로, 사람을 칭찬할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form placed before a noun, used to praise a person.

phrases.en: My grandfather is very knowledgeable about Korean food.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어른에게 쓰는 높임 활용형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The honorific form, used for elders or people you respect.

phrases.en: That person is well versed in the law.
phrases.nuance_ko: '박식하다'와 비슷한 뜻이고, 특정 분야를 깊이 아는 사람에게 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Close in meaning to '박식하다', often used for someone who knows a field deeply.

explain_en: It is a compliment for someone who has built up wide knowledge through books or study. It is usually used as '~에 박식하다', and the honorific is '박식하시다'. '해박하다' is a similar word.

t90.ax: Our teacher is really knowledgeable about history.

en: to select; to choose; to single out

examples.en: The director picked a newcomer for the lead role.

examples.ko: 대표님이 저를 새 프로젝트에 발탁해 주셨어요.
examples.en: The CEO picked me for the new project.

examples.ko: 실력 있는 선수를 발탁하려고 전국을 돌아다녀요.
examples.en: They travel all over the country to pick talented players.
Everyone wonders what the criteria for picking are.

examples.ko: 처음으로 외국인 선수를 대표팀에 발탁할 거예요.
examples.en: For the first time, they will pick a foreign player for the national team.

examples.ko: 길에서 저를 가수로 발탁한 사람이 우리 삼촌이에요.
examples.en: The person who scouted me on the street as a singer is my uncle.

explain: '발탁하다'는 윗사람이나 조직이 숨은 능력을 보고 사람을 특별히 올려 쓸 때 써요. 뽑히는 쪽에서는 '발탁되다'라고 말해요. '뽑다'보다 좋은 기회를 준다는 느낌이 있어서 칭찬하는 분위기에서 자주 써요.

phrases.en: A new actor was selected for the lead role.
phrases.nuance_ko: '발탁하다'의 피동 표현으로 뽑히는 쪽을 주어로 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The passive form, with the person who is picked as the subject.

phrases.en: The director chose a newcomer for the lead.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서 더 쉽게 쓰는 말이지만 특별한 기회를 준다는 느낌은 약해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A simpler everyday word, but it lacks the sense of giving a special chance.

phrases.en: The president picked me to be team leader.
phrases.nuance_ko: 윗사람이 나를 뽑아 준 것에 고마움을 담아 높여 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A respectful form expressing gratitude that a superior chose you.

explain_en: Active; pick from many for a key role — coach, boss. 발탁하다 is used when a superior or an organization spots hidden ability and gives the person a special role. From the chosen person's side you say 발탁되다. It feels warmer than 뽑다 because it implies a good opportunity, so it often appears in praising contexts.

dis.h: pick from many for a key role
gh: choose after review; prizes, sites, winners
pick via exam or competition; team, staff
screen and sort out by quality

p.n: 발탁하다 stresses singling someone out above others; 선발하다 suggests a selection process.

t90.ax: The CEO picked me for the new project.

examples.en: I barely make a living with this job.

examples.ko: 아들이 이제 혼자 밥벌이할 나이가 됐어요.
examples.en: My son is now old enough to earn his own living.
It is hard to make a living from translation alone.
He made a living doing deliveries during the day.

examples.ko: 어떻게든 밥벌이해야 하니까 아무 일이나 해 봐야 해요.
examples.en: I have to earn a living somehow, so I have to try any job.
These days many people make a living from YouTube.

explain: '밥벌이를 하다'처럼 '를'을 넣어도 써요. '돈을 벌다'보다 먹고살기 위해 일한다는 절실한 느낌이 있어요. 구어에서 자주 쓰고, 격식 있는 글에서는 '생계를 유지하다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: I earn my own living now too.
phrases.nuance_ko: '밥벌이하다'를 띄어 쓴 모양으로 뜻은 같고, '제 밥벌이'처럼 꾸미는 말을 넣기 쉬워요.
phrases.nuance_en: The spaced-out form of 밥벌이하다 with the same meaning; it makes it easy to add a modifier like 제 밥벌이.

phrases.example: 요즘 일이 없어서 밥벌이 걱정이 많아요.
phrases.en: I have no work lately, so I worry a lot about making a living.
phrases.nuance_ko: 먹고살 일을 걱정할 때 '밥벌이'를 명사로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses 밥벌이 as a noun when worrying about making a living.

phrases.en: He makes a living with a small shop.
phrases.nuance_ko: '밥벌이하다'보다 격식 있는 글이나 말에서 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A more formal expression than 밥벌이하다, used in writing or formal speech.

explain_en: You can also say '밥벌이를 하다' with the particle '를'. Compared with '돈을 벌다', it carries a feeling of working just to get by. It is common in speech, and in formal writing people say '생계를 유지하다'.

examples.en: My dream is to be a translator who translates books.
The translator rendered the novel into Korean.
A famous translator translated this book.
I met a translator and heard their story.

examples.ko: 좋은 번역가가 되려면 두 언어를 잘 알아야 해요.
examples.en: To be a good translator you must know both languages well.
I gave a dictionary to my translator friend.

explain: '번역가'는 글을 번역하는 사람이고, 말로 바로 옮기는 사람은 '통역사'라고 해요. 책이나 영화 자막을 번역하는 사람은 번역가라고 해요. 직업을 말할 때는 '번역가예요'라고 해요.

phrases.en: The film translator is making the subtitles.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞에 분야를 붙여서 어떤 글을 번역하는지 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put a field before it to say what kind of text the person translates.

phrases.en: I want to become a translator later.
phrases.nuance_ko: 꿈이나 직업을 말할 때 자주 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common phrase for talking about dreams or careers.

phrases.en: My older sister works as a translator at a publishing company.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 하는 직업을 말할 때 '-(으)로 일하다'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '-(으)로 일하다' to say what someone does for work now.

explain_en: 번역가 is a person who translates written text, while someone who interprets speech on the spot is a 통역사. People who translate books or film subtitles are called 번역가. When stating a job, you say 번역가예요.

examples.en: I met a patent attorney to file for a patent.
My uncle works as a patent attorney.
I heard the patent attorney exam is very difficult.
I left the trademark of the new product to a patent attorney.

examples.ko: 변리사가 되려면 어떤 공부를 해야 해요?
examples.en: What do I need to study to become a patent attorney?
The patent attorney's office is on the third floor of this building.

explain: 특허나 상표 같은 지식재산 일을 도와주는 전문직이에요. 소송이나 일반 법률 문제는 '변호사'가 맡아요.

phrases.en: I met a patent attorney to register a trademark.
phrases.nuance_ko: 특허나 상표 일로 상담할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when consulting about patents or trademarks.

phrases.en: The patent attorney's office is on the third floor of this building.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일하는 곳을 말할 때 뒤에 '사무실'을 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add 사무실 after it to name the workplace.

phrases.en: My friend is preparing for the patent attorney exam.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이 직업이 되기 위한 시험을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the exam needed to become one.

explain_en: This is a professional who helps with intellectual property such as patents and trademarks. Lawsuits and general legal matters are handled by a '변호사' (lawyer).

examples.en: My father works as an office clerk at a small company.
I saw a notice saying they're hiring an office clerk.
The office clerk is organizing documents.
I asked the school office clerk for a certificate.
Attention to detail is important in office clerk work.

examples.ko: 우리 동네 병원에는 사무원이 두 명 있어요.
examples.en: The clinic in my neighborhood has two office staff.

explain: 책상에서 서류, 접수, 회계 같은 일을 하는 사람을 직업으로 말할 때 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '회사원', '직원', '사무직'이라고 더 자주 말해요. 직접 부를 때는 '사무원님' 대신 이름이나 직함을 써요.

phrases.en: I want to work in an office job.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 아니라 사무 일의 종류를 말해요. 일상 대화에서 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the type of office work rather than the person. It is more common in daily talk.

phrases.en: My older brother is an employee at a small company.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사무원보다 넓게 회사에서 일하는 사람을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A broader word than 사무원 for anyone who works at a company.

phrases.example: 우리 회사에서 사무원을 두 명 뽑아요.
phrases.en: Our company is hiring two office clerks.
phrases.nuance_ko: 채용 이야기를 할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing when talking about hiring.

explain_en: A person doing clerical duties in an office; a specific role. It names the job of someone who does desk work such as paperwork, reception or accounting. In daily speech, people more often say '회사원', '직원' or '사무직'. When addressing someone directly, use their name or title rather than '사무원님'.

t90.ax: The office clerk is organizing documents.
